purpose: Canonical product analytics event contract for OpenClaw-developed products.

naming_policy.system_exception: campaign-visit remains hyphenated because analytics-gateway campaign reporting is built around this system event.
naming_policy.product_specificity: Do not encode product, page, or button identity in the event name. Put those details in payload fields.

applicability_policy.selection_rule: Evaluate every event's required_when against the supplied product requirements and real behavior. Applicable acquisition, interaction, activation, signup, verification, and payment events compose additively; no single product profile is a complete checklist.
applicability_policy.pageview_rule: Use the shared Umami snippet's native pageviews for required page-view measurement; do not invent a custom page-view event.
applicability_policy.interaction_rule: Require cta_click for each primary conversion placement and button_click only for analytically meaningful secondary actions, never every incidental control.
applicability_policy.not_applicable_marker: Mark missing lifecycle areas as not_applicable or pending in product metadata instead of emitting fake events.

privacy.direct_identifiers: Avoid raw personal identifiers in Umami payloads. Use non-sensitive internal IDs only when needed.

attribution_payload.source: Frontend reads window.__egbeAttribution.read(); backend persists the same first-touch fields with durable signup/payment metadata for later backend joins. Signup rows use canonical first_utm_* columns (or their camelCase ORM equivalents) so Site Gateway can discover them automatically.
attribution_payload.rule: First-touch fields remain stable for the visitor. Later touch data may be stored separately, but channel reports use first-touch by default.

delivery_policy.source_model: Separate lifecycle confirmation from Umami delivery. Backend can be the source of truth for a durable fact while the browser emits the canonical Umami event so it stays attached to the user's session timeline.
delivery_policy.browser_session_rule: Events that occur during an active user flow must be emitted with the Umami browser tracker (`window.umami.track`) after any required backend confirmation. Do not use direct backend `/api/send` as the primary delivery path for these user-session funnel events.

browser_after_backend_confirmation.rule: The backend confirms the durable state change and returns an analytics descriptor. The browser then sends the canonical event immediately or stores it in a short-lived pending queue (for example sessionStorage) and flushes it after redirect.

backend_direct.allowed_when: Use direct backend delivery only for webhook, renewal, refund, admin/system, or other out-of-session lifecycle events that have no active browser session timeline to join.
backend_direct.rule: Persist first-touch attribution with account/payment metadata so backend direct events can still be joined for channel reporting. Treat Umami {"beep":"boop"} as filtered delivery when a backend collector send is used.

delivery_policy.umami_session_note: Umami server-side sends can write aggregate events, but they may receive a different `session_id` from browser events. Use browser delivery for user-session funnel timelines.

optional_telemetry_policy.rule: Optional engagement telemetry is not part of the canonical product funnel and must not satisfy `cta_click`, `button_click`, or lifecycle event guardrails.

events.name: campaign-visit
events.required_when: A public product page has the shared analytics tracking snippet and the visitor arrives with UTM, click-id, or other explicit campaign attribution. Referrer-only traffic does not trigger this event by itself.
events.firing_rule: The shared tracking snippet emits once per attributed visit signature.

events.name: cta_click
events.required_when: A primary conversion-driving CTA exists on a public page.
events.firing_rule: Fire when the visitor clicks a primary CTA that moves them toward activation, signup, pricing, checkout, or a channel handoff.

events.name: button_click
events.required_when: A non-primary but analytically meaningful button exists.
events.firing_rule: Fire for important product or landing buttons. Do not fire for every incidental UI control.

events.name: activated
events.required_when: The product has a real first-value moment or core action completion before or after signup.
events.firing_rule: Fire when the visitor receives real product value or completes a caller-required core outcome, not when they merely click a button. Use a stable activation_type for each measured outcome and identify one type as the product's primary activation. If the outcome is created by a backend action, return a confirmed analytics descriptor and emit from the browser after success.

events.name: signup_started
events.required_when: A signup, registration, account creation, or lead-capture form exists.
events.firing_rule: Fire when a visitor intentionally enters the signup flow.

events.name: signup_submitted
events.required_when: A signup form can be submitted.
events.firing_rule: Fire immediately before or at form submit after client-side validation passes.

events.name: signup_completed
events.required_when: Signup creates a durable account, registration row, subscriber row, or accepted lead-capture row.
events.firing_rule: Confirm only after the durable write succeeds. The backend is the source of truth for completion, then the browser emits the Umami event so it joins the signup session timeline.

events.name: email_verified
events.required_when: The product requires email verification or magic-link confirmation.
events.firing_rule: Fire when a verification token is accepted and the account/email state becomes verified. Prefer browser delivery on the verification result page; use backend direct only for out-of-session verification handling.

events.name: paywall_view
events.required_when: The product has a paywall, pricing gate, upgrade gate, or paid-plan prompt.
events.firing_rule: Fire when the paywall or paid prompt becomes visible.

events.name: checkout_started
events.required_when: A real checkout session, payment link redirect, deposit, or paid-pilot checkout starts.
events.firing_rule: Confirm when the product successfully creates a dynamic checkout session or real checkout URL. Emit the Umami event from the browser before redirect or queue it and flush before navigation.

events.name: purchase
events.required_when: A Stripe checkout/payment event confirms successful payment for the product.
events.firing_rule: Confirm from the payment webhook or backend status check after idempotently accepting a paid Stripe event. Expose a pending descriptor to the owning checkout-success browser and emit the canonical Umami event there. Use Stripe/OS payment metrics, not server-only Umami delivery, for complete financial totals.

events.name: subscription_renewed
events.required_when: The product supports subscriptions and receives renewal/payment lifecycle events.
events.firing_rule: Fire when a subscription renewal invoice is paid and applied idempotently.

events.name: subscription_canceled
events.required_when: The product supports subscriptions and receives cancellation/deletion lifecycle events.
events.firing_rule: Fire when a cancellation is accepted and entitlement state changes or is scheduled to end. Use browser delivery for user-initiated cancel flows; use backend direct for webhook/admin/system cancellations.

events.name: refund
events.required_when: The product and payment gateway support refund lifecycle events.
events.firing_rule: Fire only when a refund is confirmed and applied idempotently.

validation_policy.setup: Verify the analytics site exists and OS tracking config is available.
validation_policy.wiring: Verify the app shell contains the tracking snippet or public analytics env wiring.
validation_policy.behavior: Drive real product flows and intercept/mock analytics delivery to verify canonical event names and payloads without writing synthetic product events to production stats.
validation_policy.observed: Use real stats from real users for reporting and channel-level iteration decisions.
